title: Neil Peart - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 167,433. Neil Ellwood Peart, born 12 September 1952, Hamilton, Ontario; died 7 January 2020, Santa Monica, California, of glioblastoma, aged 67. Sticks, a practice pad and lessons at 13; a kit at 14 and lessons with Don George at the Peninsula Conservatory of Music; first band the Eternal Triangle; Mumblin' Sumpthin', the Majority; about 18 months in London from 18; Hush on his return. Joined Rush 29 July 1974, replacing John Rutsey; became its lyricist. 'Early style was rooted in hard rock', influences Keith Moon, Ginger Baker, John Bonham; later jazz and big band, Gene Krupa and Buddy Rich; also named Bill Bruford, Phil Collins, Michael Giles, Carl Palmer, Steve Gadd, Stewart Copeland, Billy Cobham, Pete Thomas; the Who first inspired him. Solos with exotic percussion and long odd-meter passages; 'The Waltz' a typical ostinato. Freddie Gruber's pupil from 1994: revamped his style with jazz and swing; traditional grip in the mid 1990s (A Work in Progress, Test for Echo), then mainly matched again. Played the 1991 Buddy Rich Memorial Scholarship Concert; produced and played on Burning for Buddy (1994, 1997); lessons with Peter Erskine from early 2007. Drums with Rush: Slingerland, Tama, Ludwig, DW. Zildjian A and Wuhan china to the early 2000s, then Sabian Paragon. Simmons and Akai samplers from Grace Under Pressure; Roland V-Drums in the 2000s; malletKAT. Percussion from the late 1970s: orchestra bells, tubular bells, wind chimes, crotales, timbales, timpani, gong, temple blocks, bell tree, triangle, cowbells. Rotating riser; 360-degree kit from the Grace Under Pressure tour. Modern Drummer Hall of Fame 1983, the youngest; 'the Professor'. 'I am no one's disciple' (1993).

title: Rush (band) - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 246,062. Formed August 1968 in Willowdale, Toronto (Lifeson, Rutsey, Jeff Jones; Lee soon after). Rutsey's last gig 25 July 1974; Peart joined 29 July. Terry Brown re-recorded the debut and began 'a ten-year partnership'. A Farewell to Kings and Hemispheres at Rockfield, Wales. Grace Under Pressure co-produced by Peter Henderson; Power Windows and Hold Your Fire, Peter Collins; Presto and Roll the Bones, Rupert Hine; Counterparts and Test for Echo, Peter Collins; Vapor Trails, Paul Northfield; Snakes & Arrows and Clockwork Angels, Nick Raskulinecz. Live: All the World's a Stage (1976, Massey Hall), Exit...Stage Left (1981), A Show of Hands (1989). With Moving Pictures 'Rush's popularity reached its pinnacle': No. 1 in Canada, No. 3 in the US. Peart's percussion broadened to 'triangles, glockenspiel, timpani, and chimes'; Simmons from Grace Under Pressure; jazz and swing from Freddie Gruber on Test for Echo. 1997-98: the deaths of his daughter and wife, 'consider me retired'; back 2001. R40 tour 8 May to 1 August 2015, the last. Rock and Roll Hall of Fame 18 April 2013.

title: Cheech Iero, 'Neil Peart Interview', Modern Drummer, April/May 1980 (transcript at 2112.net)
notes: Keith Moon 'gave me a new idea of the freedom and that there was no need to be a fundamentalist'; names Bruford, Carl Palmer, Phil Collins, Michael Giles, Kevin Ellman, Tommy Aldridge. First teacher 'Paul' (surname not recalled), who taught him rudimental and flashy material such as crossovers. Traditional grip for rudimental work, 'that's the way I learned it', but 'not the best way'; matched otherwise, the butt end of light sticks for impact. Kit refinished in mahogany by the Percussion Center, Fort Wayne: 'I was trying to achieve a Rosewood'. 13-inch hats for his 'hi-hat punctuation'; 'My cymbals are chosen for the length of decay that I want'; cracks 16s and 18s. Concert toms, tubular bells, crotales, glockenspiel, timpani, a gong stand; 'I don't feel comfortable with wires and electronic things'. Listens to the vocal and frames it; fills 'refresh' a song night to night; 'I play with a lot of open drums, open concert toms', Evans heads; both bass drum heads on live with a small hole. Odd times in 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, some 21-beat bars; first understood meter from Genesis; does not count except through pauses. The solo 'like a song': an introduction, movements, 'comic relief', a build.

title: Susan Alexander, 'Neil Peart: Rush Release', Rhythm, March 1987 (transcript at 2112.net)
notes: 'The first thing my teacher played for me was a drum battle record between Buddy Rich and Gene Krupa'; 'I think Gene Krupa was a really important influence because of the abandon with which he played'; 'I think his rock 'n' roll heir was probably Keith Moon ... even though Keith Moon showed even more abandon and was more sloppy ... It opened me up'; 'Drummers like Michael Giles of King Crimson, Bill Bruford with Yes, Carl Palmer with Emerson, Lake and Palmer and Phil Collins with Genesis were all important drummers to me. They set such a high standard of technical ability but with the excitement that rock drumming has.' 'I think a lot of my appeal lies in the fact that I overplay like crazy and I'm allowed to, within the context of this band.' 'years and years went into searching for a better time sense'; odd times, 'let's try it in 7 or 11, or 9'; fills written beyond him and practised until recorded; electronics 'less dynamic', making his fills 'a little more linear'; 'my main rhythmic foundation is still an acoustic bass drum and an acoustic snare'; the kit as 'my own personal orchestra'.

title: Neil Peart, 'Neil Peart On Drum Solos', Rhythm, March and April 2014 (transcript at 2112.net)
notes: Read as a summary with quotes. Max Roach's The Drum Also Waltzes has served his practice and soloing for about twenty years: it 'took a long time to get 'free' over the waltz time, but now I can flail around at will, in any tempo or time signature'; the bass drum and hi-hat bring in the 'xaxado ostinato', 'a more recent fascination'. 'polyrhythmic thinking' in splitting the solo into sections; the Binary Love Theme moves 'from waltz to 4/4, then to 7/8'. 'improvisation has been a major aspiration for me'; elements 'deliberately not allowed to become fixed'. 'my late teacher' Freddie Gruber; 'my first inspiration to play drums was the movie The Gene Krupa Story'; of Buddy Rich, 'back then I couldn't even understand what Buddy was doing'. Electronics as 'satellites' round the main kit; keyboard percussion in the late '70s and '80s.

title: Don Zulaica, 'Mean Mean Stride: The Drums of Neil Peart', DRUM!, October 2005 (transcript at 2112.net)
notes: At 14 a red sparkle Stewart kit; Slingerland Gene Krupa sticks, butt end; at about 16 a Rogers in gray ripple with two bass drums. 1974: chrome Slingerland, two 22x14 bass drums, two 13x9 and a 14x10 rack tom, a 16x16 floor tom; Zildjian 13 New Beat hats, 16, 18, 20 crashes, 22 Ping ride; 'Old Number One', a copper-finish 14x5.5 snare. Caress of Steel: single-headed concert toms 6, 8, 10, 12. 2112 to Hemispheres: black chrome Slingerland, 'Vibrafibed', 24x14 bass drums, 12x8 and 15x12 toms, 18x16 floor tom; temple blocks, tubular bells, brass timbales, wind chimes, bell tree, triangles, glockenspiel; Hemispheres added crotales, Wuhan and Zildjian chinas, a gong and a 28-inch tympanum. Permanent Waves and Moving Pictures: Tama Superstars, dark rosewood stain, brass-plated hardware; for Moving Pictures the brass timbales became wood and the tympanum two single-headed Tama gong bass drums, 20x14 and 22x14. Signals: Candy Apple Red, brass hardware, thin-shell Tama Artstar prototypes. Grace Under Pressure: four red Simmons pads, an SDS-V, a Clap Trap; one 13-inch metal timbale; the riser not yet in use, so at Radio City he faced the back of the stage. Hold Your Fire: Ludwig in opalescent white; a malletKAT replaced the woodblocks, crotales and glockenspiel. Counterparts and Test for Echo: traditional grip after Freddie Gruber, DW in Blood Red Sparkle.

title: Drumspy, 'Neil Peart Drum Kit Setups'
notes: 1979-81 Tama: 'custom rosewood finish' (a mahogany trying to be rosewood), brass-plated hardware, two 24-inch bass drums, concert toms 6, 8, 10, 12, closed toms 12, 13, 15, 18, a 5.5x14 Slingerland Artist; Zildjian (6 and 8 splashes, 8 and 10 by Moving Pictures), 13 hats, two 16s, 18 and 20 crashes, 22 ride, 18 pang, a 20 China; timbales, orchestra bells, tubular bells, wind chimes, temple blocks, cowbells, triangle, bell tree, crotales, Burma bell; timpani and gong replaced by two gong bass drums at Moving Pictures. 1982-86 Tama Artstar prototype: 'candy apple red', brass-plated hardware, two 24s, the same toms, gong bass drums 20 and 22, the Slingerland snare refinished candy apple red; Zildjian and Wuhan; Simmons from 1984 (three tom modules, one snare, a Clap Trap), SDS-7 from 1985. Later finishes: Ludwig white opalescent (1987), plum (1989), Blue Shadow, Black Cherry; DW red sparkle (1996); black and gold (2004); Aztec Red (2007); the Time Machine kit (2010); R40 (2015).

title: Rush is a Band, 'Neil Peart's red Tama drum kit up for auction', 7 June 2012 (Julien's Auctions lot 28533)
notes: The listing: 'A Tama Superstar drum kit, custom made for Neil Peart'; the blog calls it a red Tama Art Star; used to record three Rush albums and on the tours after, in nine music videos and the concert video Grace Under Pressure Tour 1984; given away in a Modern Drummer contest in 1987; sold for $35,000.

title: Burning for Buddy: A Tribute to the Music of Buddy Rich - Wikipedia
notes: Released 4 October 1994 on Atlantic; recorded May 1994 at the Power Station, New York; produced by Neil Peart. Eighteen tracks with the Buddy Rich Big Band, a drummer each; Peart plays track 6, Cotton Tail. Max Roach plays The Drum Also Waltzes, parts 1 and 2.

title: YYZ (instrumental) - Wikipedia
notes: The intro spells the Toronto airport code Y-Y-Z in Morse code, in 10/8; Peart said the rhythm 'stuck in my head'. Exit...Stage Left (1981) has his drum solo as an interlude inside it. Nominated for the Grammy for Best Rock Instrumental Performance (1982), lost to the Police's Behind My Camel.

title: Mike Portnoy - Wikipedia
notes: 'he cited Neil Peart, Ringo Starr, Phil Collins, John Bonham, and Keith Moon as influences'; Rush among the bands of his youth.

Peart: tall and lean, short dark brown hair a little wavy on top, clean-shaven, a loose white T-shirt with short sleeves (a small dark print low on the chest in one shot), no headphones.
